# SK2004 — Typed equality has no matching object equality

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A type implements `IEquatable<Self>` without overriding Equals(object).

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

Typed and object-based consumers can otherwise disagree about equality. A class can compare equal through `IEquatable<T>` while its object equality and hash code still use identity; structs can similarly diverge from their fallback field comparison.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
class Key : IEquatable<Key> { public bool Equals(Key? other) => other is not null; }
```

Write:

```csharp
class Key : IEquatable<Key> { public bool Equals(Key? other) => other is not null; public override bool Equals(object? other) => other is Key key && Equals(key); public override int GetHashCode() => 0; }
```

## When it does not fire

Only the framework `IEquatable<T>` with the containing type itself as T is recognized. Records and inherited object-equality overrides are accepted, and partial types report once. Types already overriding Equals(object) are left to compiler diagnostics for a missing GetHashCode. This does not prove that existing equality or hashing implementations are consistent, and no fix can infer the identity fields.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK2004.severity`
